title: Connect Fibre rolls out Wi-Fi 7 across all broadband plans
content: Connect Fibre, a community-focused full fibre broadband provider, has launched Wi-Fi 7 across all its contracted packages. After thorough testing with top global manufacturers, the company is bringing next-gen tech to customers at no extra cost, sticking to its fair-pricing promise. The upgrade sets a new standard in the UK fibre market, making cutting-edge connectivity accessible without premium fees. Alongside Wi-Fi 7, Connect Fibre offers flexibility with 24-month contracts for lower rates or 12-month options for shorter commitments. The provider has also boosted its entry-level plan from 150Mbps to 250Mbps at no additional cost (on a 24-month deal), while its top-tier package now hits 2000Mbps. What Wi-Fi 7 brings Wi-Fi 7 uses advanced radio tech and new frequencies for faster, interference-free connections. Benefits include: Faster speeds : Multi-gigabit performance beats Wi-Fi 6, perfect for streaming and gaming. Lower latency : Reduced delays enhance gaming, AR/VR, and video calls. More capacity : Supports multiple devices with 8×8 MU-MIMO, ideal for smart homes. Stefan Stanislawski, CEO of Connect Fibre, said: “The launch of Wi-Fi 7 is a game-changer, and we’re proud to be leading the charge in bringing this cutting-edge technology to our customers. At Connect Fibre, innovation and customer experience are at the heart of everything we do. We believe everyone should have access to the best possible connectivity without barriers or premium pricing. With Wi-Fi 7, we’re not just keeping up with the future – we’re shaping it.”

title: Daisy Communications Strikes Long-Term Partnership with AllPoints Fibre Networks
content: Daisy Communications has signed a long-term strategic partnership with AllPoints Fibre Networks (APFN), securing access to a national full-fibre network through APFN’s aquila wholesale platform. With aquila , Daisy can instantly connect to millions of premises via a single, API-first platform—eliminating the complexity of managing multiple fibre networks. As part of the deal, Daisy will also acquire APFN’s B2B direct customer base, previously managed under the Giganet brand. Both companies have confirmed that customers will see no change to their service levels or pricing, while also gaining access to Daisy’s wider product suite and industry-leading support. The partnership takes effect immediately, and customers moving to Daisy have already been informed. Jarlath Finnegan, Group CEO at AllPoints Fibre Networks, said: “The Daisy deal marks another key milestone for APFN. Daisy now has access to the UK’s largest full-fibre wholesale network, benefiting the customers who have supported us along the way. We want to thank them and look forward to continuing that support through Daisy in the years ahead.” Dave McGinn, CEO at Daisy Communications, added: “We’re excited to bring the UK’s largest full-fibre wholesale network to our customers through this partnership. We also welcome the new businesses joining Daisy as part of the deal and look forward to working with them to keep Britain connected.”

title: Voiceflex Partners with Vorboss to Strengthen Business Connectivity
content: Voiceflex has joined forces with Vorboss, London’s leading business ethernet fibre provider, to support partners with connectivity growth in the capital. Reliable connectivity is essential for modern businesses. Without a solid connection to the cloud, operations slow down or stop entirely. Many of Voiceflex’s services run in real-time, making uptime and performance critical. A system is only as strong as its weakest link. Partnering with a specialist fibre provider gives businesses access to high-speed, low-latency internet built for handling data-heavy applications, cloud services, and communication tools. Fibre isn’t just faster than traditional broadband—it’s more stable, scalable, and designed to support growing demands. Paul Taylor, CCO of Voiceflex, said: “We’re really impressed by their uptime stats, but even more so by the money-back service credits. If an outage goes beyond four minutes, an automatic credit is applied at the end of the month. That level of accountability is rare.” For businesses that need dependable, high-quality connectivity, this partnership makes a lot of sense.

title: Quickline Rolls Out Full Fibre to Hard-to-Reach Homes in Lincolnshire & East Yorkshire
content: Thousands of rural homes and businesses across Lincolnshire and the East Riding of Yorkshire are finally getting the broadband speeds they deserve. Quickline is delivering full fibre broadband as part of the government-backed Project Gigabit, bringing next-generation connectivity to communities that have long been left behind. Since securing the contract in summer 2024, Quickline has already connected nearly 850 funded homes and businesses to gigabit-capable broadband. The first areas to benefit include the villages of Ruskington, Ancaster, and Burgh le Marsh in the south of Lincolnshire. But this is just the start. Work is now pushing further north, with North Cave and Gilberdyke in the East Riding of Yorkshire next in line. Holme on Spalding Moor will follow soon after. The rollout is moving fast—just six months after securing the contract, the first homes were live, and four months after breaking ground, residents were able to connect. In total, the contract will bring full fibre to nearly 72,000 properties. On top of that, another 50,000 premises will benefit from Quickline’s separate commercial rollout. This means tens of thousands of people in rural areas will finally have access to reliable, high-speed internet. Dan Hague, Project Delivery Director at Quickline, said: “Bringing high-speed broadband to rural communities is what we do best. From day one, the focus has been on getting results quickly, and connecting over 800 premises in just a few months is a huge milestone. Our teams are working tirelessly to bring reliable broadband to areas that have struggled for too long.” Telecoms Minister Sir Chris Bryant added: “Poor connectivity has been a major challenge for people living and working in rural Lincolnshire and East Yorkshire. Whether it’s remote NHS consultations or simply staying in touch with loved ones, fast broadband is essential. Thanks to this government-funded rollout, thousands of homes and businesses will now have access to the fastest speeds on the market, boosting the local economy and improving everyday life.” Homes and businesses in the rollout areas can now book their installation and get connected. The digital divide is closing—one village at a time.

title: Gigaclear Begins Project Gigabit Build to Connect 9,500 Oxfordshire Premises
content: Gigaclear has begun work on Project Gigabit in Oxfordshire, aiming to connect around 9,500 homes and businesses to full-fibre broadband. The £25.4m government-funded initiative targets hard-to-reach areas, with Gigaclear installing over 250km of new ducting—50% of which will utilise existing infrastructure. Nathan Rundle, CEO of Gigaclear, said: “Our mission is to bring full-fibre broadband to rural communities, and Project Gigabit is key to making that happen. As an Oxfordshire-based business, we’re committed to improving digital access in the county and delivering fast, reliable connectivity to local residents.” Telecoms Minister Sir Chris Bryant added: “Many communities in Oxfordshire have been excluded from the benefits of fast broadband. Through Project Gigabit, we’re closing those digital gaps and moving closer to our goal of full gigabit coverage by 2030.” Work is now underway, with completion expected by November 2026. Project Gigabit is part of the government’s strategy to ensure no rural community is left behind, delivering the same digital opportunities already available in larger towns and cities.
